focus.title: Does Conductor open with no signal on your phone?
focus.detail: Conductor should open from your Home Screen even in Airplane Mode, and we want to know which phones manage it. On your phone, open the app (<https://quidam2k.github.io/conductor/>) and note the build number at the bottom of the home screen. Add it to your Home Screen (iPhone: Share → Add to Home Screen; Android: browser menu → Add to Home screen or Install app). Close the browser, turn on Airplane Mode, and tap the new Conductor icon. Bonus, with signal back: open <https://quidam2k.github.io/conductor/nope> and check you get a short "Page not found" page. Tell us in a GitHub issue: your phone model, system version, the build number, and whether the app opened offline.

focus.title: iPhone on iOS 26: do the beeps, voice cues and the new robot voice keep playing with the screen locked?
focus.detail: We've confirmed beeps and recorded voice cues on iOS 18 with the phone locked in a pocket, but not yet on iOS 26. New in build v73: typed cues are read by a built-in robot voice that goes into the same locked-screen track, and nobody has tried it on a locked iPhone yet. On an iPhone running iOS 26, open the Help Us Test page (<https://quidam2k.github.io/conductor/test/>) and follow the steps; then also open the app, paste a two-line typed event (for example `0:30 Freeze` and `1:00 Unfreeze`), tap Practice, lock the phone for 3 minutes and listen. Tip: in Safari tap Share → Add to Home Screen and open Conductor from that icon (Safari's new bottom toolbar can cover the Go Live button). Tell us in a GitHub issue: your iOS version, the build number at the bottom of the home screen, whether the beeps, voice cues and robot voice played with the screen locked, and whether they were on time.

focus.title: Five minutes with your phone: does it work in your pocket?
focus.detail: Open the Help Us Test page (<https://quidam2k.github.io/conductor/test/>) on your phone and follow the steps. It checks whether Conductor's audio keeps playing with the screen locked on YOUR device. Nothing is sent unless you choose to send it. Tell us your phone model and what you heard in a GitHub issue — iPhones and older Androids are especially useful.

focus.title: Lowest lift of all: rate the touchstones we've collected
focus.detail: We've gathered a big pile of cultural touchstones — recognizable lines that scripts pull from — and we need help separating the wheat from the chaff. Open the rating page (<https://quidam2k.github.io/conductor/rate.html>) and give a quick 1–5 stars to the ones that jump out at you, good or bad. Don't rate all of them — please don't. Skip the middle: 5 stars for a line almost anyone would know and love, 1 star for one that falls flat, and leave the forgettable ones unrated (that's a signal too). Even five ratings genuinely help. No download, no typing — just tap stars and submit the prefilled issue it builds for you.
